records.title: A registered comparison of lunchtime walking routes
records.authorReasoning: Random route allocation is separated from volunteer recruitment. The worked answer distinguishes a complete route package from greenery alone, participant expectancy from assessor masking, and immediate reported restoration from lasting well-being. Registration is treated as transparency rather than guaranteed validity.
alternativeInterpretations: A route effect could reflect expectations, light or noise; library volunteers limit transfer to other settings.

alternativeInterpretations: Additional independent recruitment chains widen access but do not convert snowball sampling into random sampling.

records.title: An identifiable success story in a small walking group
records.authorReasoning: The proposed bus-route explanation is explicitly challenged by simultaneous changes in leadership and meeting time. alternativeInterpretations: Different sources can disagree productively; publishing raw records would conflict with protecting recognisable members.

records.authorReasoning: Naturally occurring ages cannot be randomly allocated. Standardised task conditions do not remove cohort experience. The evaluation separates age differences from within-person development and accessibility/familiarity from ability.
alternativeInterpretations: A longitudinal extension changes the inference problem but brings practice, attrition and historical-context limitations.

records.title: Watching planning develop without counting the same skill twice
records.authorReasoning: Following the same adults addresses within-person change, but repeating the identical task supports a practice explanation. Clarification requests are not assumed to measure dependence. Consistent coding, attrition and separation from coordinator appraisal are treated distinctly.
alternativeInterpretations: Fewer clarification requests might reflect task familiarity, confidence or reluctance, rather than developed planning independence.

records.authorReasoning: Operational event definitions support consistency but not automatic construct validity. Tool-offer opportunities, interaction sequence, camera field, coder acquaintance and participant meanings provide specific challenges to a count-based relationship interpretation.
alternativeInterpretations: A fluent cooperative pair may make fewer explicit offers; a high offer count could accompany misunderstanding.

records.title: Device switching and learning in an evening language course
records.authorReasoning: No switching behaviour is assigned. Work demands, prior experience and difficult learning can jointly shape diary entries and task results. Task scope, diary reactivity, limited data collection and omitted entries are discussed without direct SL data analysis.
alternativeInterpretations: Switching may follow learning difficulty rather than cause it; missing diary entries cannot be coded automatically as no switching.

records.title: A single learner whose archive contains only finished work
records.authorReasoning: Finished products are not a complete record of strategy or abandoned work. Source variety is distinguished from independence. Teacher and learner perspectives, a single new observation and recognisable creative material bound the account of development.
alternativeInterpretations: A prospective draft archive would improve future evidence but cannot reconstruct the unrecorded historical process.
